about.title: Mount Shasta Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Mount Shasta sits along Interstate 5, a corridor that carries a steady mix of local traffic, freight, and travelers passing through Siskiyou County. Public crash records show injury collisions clustering on I-5 Northbound, I-5 Southbound, and N Mt Shasta Boulevard, with Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. seeing more reported crashes than other times. Whether you were rear-ended near a Boulevard intersection or caught in a highway collision, the aftermath can mean medical appointments, missed work, and an insurance adjuster asking questions before you've had time to think. We're a personal injury team ready to evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no cost for a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless your claim results in a recovery.
commonInjuries: Cuts, bruising, and soft tissue damage

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Fault Rules Can Work in Your Favor
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible, you may still recover a share of damages. We can help make sure your portion of fault isn't overstated by the other side's insurer.

items.title: Your Time to File Is Limited
items.desc: Most car accident injury claims in California must be filed within two years, but claims involving a government entity — like a road defect or a public vehicle — can require notice in as little as six months. Getting an evaluation early helps preserve your options before a deadline passes.

items.title: What You Say Early Can Affect Your Claim
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, and those statements can be used to limit what you're offered later. We can advise you on what to say — and what to avoid — before you speak with any insurer.

items.question: I was in a crash on I-5 near Mount Shasta — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical attention even if injuries seem minor, since some symptoms show up days later. Try to document the scene, get contact and insurance information, and avoid giving a recorded statement to any insurance company until you've spoken with an attorney. We can provide a free case evaluation.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial case review is free, and we work on contingency, which means we only get paid if your case results in a recovery. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.

items.question: Do I have a case if the crash happened on a city street like N Mt Shasta Boulevard instead of the highway?
items.answer: Location on its own doesn't determine whether you have a claim — what matters is how the collision happened and the injuries involved. We can review the specifics, whether it occurred on I-5 or a local boulevard, and let you know your realistic options.

items.question: What if I think I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California's comparative fault rule allows you to seek compensation even if you share some responsibility for the crash, though your recovery may be adjusted accordingly. It's worth having us review the details rather than assuming fault rules you out.
